title: Unification of Egypt
summary: Around 3100 BCE, Upper and Lower Egypt were politically unified into a single territorial state under King Narmer (traditionally identified with Menes), founding ancient Egypt's First Dynasty. The iconic Narmer Palette discovered at Hierakonpolis depicts the king wearing both the White Crown of Upper Egypt and the Red Crown of Lower Egypt, commemorating the emergence of the world's earliest unified territorial nation-state, which centralized governance along the Nile Valley from the Delta to the First Cataract.

uncertainty.note: Traditionally dated to c. 3100 BCE; Bayesian radiocarbon modeling by Dee et al. (2013) places the accession of King Aha and the foundation of the state at 3111–3045 BCE (68% probability).

importance.justification: The unification of Upper and Lower Egypt under the First Dynasty established the earliest continuous territorial nation-state in human history and institutionalized pharaonic kingship.
